# Why Bodhisattva belongs in your address bar

Every address bar is a choice. When you type ​**Bodhisattva**, you are not typing a novelty; you are restoring a name that the early DNS, built for English typewriters, could not carry. The plain ASCII form *boddhisattva* is a leftover of ‌that constraint, not the name itself. This post is the long version of the restoration: where the name comes from, how the Devanagari tradition wrote it, how it is pronounced, what the ‌myths and the material record preserve, and why its Unicode form now lives as a working domain. The claim throughout is simple — the original spelling is not decoration. It is the ​name.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Bodhisattva
- **ASCII form:** boddhisattva
- **Meaning:** "'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the sake of all beings"
- **Domain of influence:** Enlightenment Being, Compassion
- **Pantheon:** Buddhist
- **Restoration:** ​ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** बोधिसत्त्व (Devanagari)

## Overview

**Bodhisattva** (*boddhisattva*) — Enlightenment Being, Compassion · 'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the sake of all beings — belongs to the Buddhist tradition, ​where it is catalogued under the domain "Enlightenment Being, Compassion". The name means "'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the sake of all beings".

**Bodhisattva** is enlightenment being, compassion. The name ​means "'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the sake of all beings" and belongs to the buddhist tradition.

PuniCodex restores the name as **Bodhisattva** and serves its temple at [its temple](https://punicodex.com/boddhisattva/). ​The restoration needs no distinctive letters or diacritics its ASCII form would lose. The plain ASCII form *boddhisattva* survives as a modern convenience imposed by the early domain-name system; the restoration, not ‌the fallback, is the form the project defends as philologically complete.

## The Name

The name is attested in Devanagari as **बोधिसत्त्व**. Etymologically it means "'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the ​sake of all beings".

The ASCII form *boddhisattva* survives only because the early domain-name system could not carry diacritics; it is a technological compromise, not an ancient spelling. The Unicode restoration **Bodhisattva** ​recovers the full diacritic detail of the scholarly transliteration directly in the address bar. The restoration needs no distinctive letters or diacritics its ASCII form would lose.

The letter-by-letter transformation runs:

- **b** ‌→ **B** — Same, capitalized
- **o** → **o** — Same
- **d** → **d** — Same
- **d** → **h** — Special character
- **h** → **i** — Special character
- **i** → **s** — Special ​character
- **s** → **a** — Special character
- **a** → **t** — Special character
- **t** → **t** — Same
- **t** → **v** — Special character
- **v** → **a** — Special character
- **a** → ‌**—** — Dropped

## The Original Script

The name is preserved in Devanagari as **बोधिसत्त्व**.

The scholarly transliteration is *Bodhisattva*.

The rendering proceeds step by step:

- Sanskrit Bodhisattva is written in Devanagari as ​बोधिसत्त्व
- IAST transliteration maps each Devanagari vowel and consonant to a Latin equivalent
- Macrons mark long vowels (ā, ī, ū); dots beneath consonants mark retroflex articulation (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ṣ)

## Pronunciation

The ‌reconstructed pronunciation of the name is **/boddhisattva/** — Restored scholarly form.

Phoneme by phoneme:

- **boddhisattva** — The canonical restored form Bodhisattva.

For the modern speaker, the closest approximation is: Say "boddhisattva" with ​the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Bodhisattva".

The ASCII form "boddhisattva" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Bodhisattva" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

The pronunciation given above reconstructs the ​sound world in which Bodhisattva was invoked. Modern speakers should not expect exact identity with ancient phonology; the reconstruction is a scholarly compass, not a performance prescription. The restoration Bodhisattva keeps the ​prosodic information visible even when the name is typed in plain ASCII.

## Mythology

The stories of Bodhisattva place enlightenment being, compassion at the center of a living mythological world.

### Origins (Myth)

Bodhisattva ​appears in buddhist tradition as enlightenment being, compassion. The name's meaning, "'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the sake of all beings", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

### Worship and ​Memory (Cult)

Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Bodhisattva in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

The myths of Bodhisattva survive in fragments, summaries, and later ‌retellings. Each version reflects the interests of its tellers — poets, priests, philosophers, and scholars. The PuniCodex entry does not privilege a single version; it gathers the attestations so that readers can ​compare them. The restoration Bodhisattva gives the figure a stable name around which these variants orbit.

### An Awakening-Being, Not Yet a Buddha (The Word)

The word is a compound: **bodhi**, awakening, plus ‌**sattva**, being — "one whose essence is awakening." In the Pāli canon *bodhisatta* is a technical term for **the Buddha before his awakening**: the *Nidānakathā* and the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14) use ​it of Gotama's past lives, from the bodhisatta enthroned in Tuṣita down to the last birth at Lumbinī. The Mahāyāna inverted the lens: the bodhisattva is no longer the road one man ‌walked but a **vocation open to all** — one who deliberately defers final nirvāṇa until the grass of beings is dry, in the Sanskrit formula of the *Kāraṇḍavyūha*. The compound thus carries ​an entire schism in six syllables: the earlier tradition's biography against the later tradition's program. An awakening-being is the answer of a religion to its own founder's success: **if one man woke, ‌the door was never locked.**

### The Promise That Builds a Bridge (The Vow)

Everything begins with a vow. The *Gaṇḍavyūha Sūtra* — the final book of the *Avataṃsaka* — sends the pilgrim ​Sudhana through fifty-three teachers and ends inside Maitreya's tower, where past vows stand visible as architecture, each floor a former life; the *praṇidhāna*, "may I not sit on awakening's seat until every ‌being is freed," is the bodhisattva's founding act. Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* (8th c.) gives the vow its classic liturgy: "For as long as space endures, and for as long as beings remain, may ​I too abide, to dispel the misery of the world." The jātakas test the vow against the body itself — Prince Śibi giving his eyes to the hawk (Jātaka 499), Vessantara giving ​away his wife and children (Jātaka 547). The mythic kernel: a promise made not to a god but to the **uncountable future** — compassion as a contract written across lifetimes, signed before ‌any power existed that could enforce it.

### From Joyful to Dharma-Cloud (The Ten Stages)

The *Daśabhūmikasūtra* maps the bodhisattva career as ten **bhūmis**, each a world of its own. *Pramuditā*, Joyful: the ‌first glimpse, irreversible; *Vimalā*, Stainless, where the ten courses of action are purified; *Prabhākarī*, Luminous, where the factors of awakening blaze; *Arciṣmatī*, Blazing; *Sudurjayā*, Difficult-to-Conquer; *Abhimukhī*, Facing — the turn toward suchness; ‌*Dūraṅgamā*, Gone-Afar; *Acalā*, Immovable, where nothing mundane can shake the vow; *Sādhumatī*, Good-Intelligence; and *Dharmameghā*, Dharma-Cloud, where Buddhas of the ten directions pour consecration from their crowns and the bodhisattva can rain ​the Dharma like a storm. The scheme seeded every later system — the five Maitreya treatises' summaries, the Tibetan graded paths, the Huayan's own rounds. Its meaning: enlightenment is not a moment ​but a **landscape**, surveyed in advance so that travelers can know exactly where they stand.

## Symbols & Iconography

The iconography associated with Bodhisattva concentrates in a small set of recurring attributes, each ‌a compressed statement about the name:

- **Name** — The restored form Bodhisattva, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.
- **Domain** — Enlightenment Being, Compassion

Symbols function as a visual shorthand: they allow devotees and ​artists to recognize Bodhisattva across media and centuries. The attributes listed above are not decorative; each one encodes a claim about power, identity, or function. The restored spelling Bodhisattva carries the same ​precision in textual form.

- **The lotus** — Untouched by the mud it grows from — the bodhisattva in the world but not of its stain; also Padmasambhava's birthplace, the word made landscape
- ‌**The sword of wisdom** — Mañjuśrī's blade cutting through ignorance — insight wielded not for oneself but to clear the road for others
- **The water flask and willow** — Guanyin's healing emblems ​— the nectar of compassion poured drop by drop onto specific suffering
- **The moon in water** — The bodhisattva's presence as reflection — appearing to beings in whatever form frees them, without ​ever leaving the empty sky
- **The staff that shakes the six realms** — Kṣitigarbha's iron khakkhara — its rings wake the dead; his vow keeps him in hell's doorway until it is ‌empty

## Archaeology & Evidence

No monument, inscription, or artifact in the current PuniCodex corpus is yet assigned to Bodhisattva with certainty. That absence should be read honestly: for a Buddhist name of this ​type the material record is expected to be thin, and the primary evidence remains the textual testimony gathered in the Scholarly Sources section.

Were such evidence to surface, it would take recognizable ‌forms: votive or dedicatory inscriptions naming बोधिसत्त्व, sanctuary or cult remains tied to enlightenment being and iconography matching its traditional attributes (name and domain). Each candidate would be weighed against the reconstructed ​form of the name before entering the scholarly record.

## Realm & Domain

**Bodhisattva** is enlightenment being, compassion. The name means "'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the sake of all beings" ​and belongs to the buddhist tradition.

### Sacred Name

The restoration Bodhisattva returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

### Enlightenment Being

Central domain: enlightenment being, compassion.

### Living Tradition

Honored in buddhist myth, cult, and ​cultural memory.

### Unicode Restoration

Preserved as a flagship temple despite the unregistrable plain-ASCII form.

### The Vow

Praṇidhāna — 'may I not sit on awakening's seat until every being is freed' — the ​founding act of the bodhisattva career.

### The Ten Stages

The Daśabhūmikasūtra's bhūmis — from Joyful to Dharma-Cloud — enlightenment surveyed as a climbable landscape.

### The Perfections

The six pāramitās — giving, morality, ‌patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom — the curriculum every vow must pass through.

### The Exemplars

Avalokiteśvara hearing the world's cries, Kṣitigarbha vowing the hells be emptied — compassion walking in person.

## Across Cultures

‌Within the Buddhist tradition, closely related names in the corpus include [[akshobhya|Akṣobhya]], [[amitabha|Amitābha]], [[amoghasiddhi|Amoghasiddhi]], [[arhat|Arhat]], [[asanga|Asanga]], and [[avalokiteshvara|Avalokiteśvara]].

Cross-cultural identifications are rarely one-to-one. Bodhisattva may be likened to figures in neighboring traditions ​without being identical to them. The PuniCodex crosslink index records these resonances as relationships, not equations. The restored form Bodhisattva makes such comparisons possible across language boundaries.

## Cultural Legacy

Bodhisattva remains a ‌touchstone for understanding buddhist religion, art, and identity.

The modern afterlife of Bodhisattva includes scholarly editions, artistic adaptations, and popular references. Each reuse renegotiates the figure’s meaning for a new audience. The ​PuniCodex temple participates in that afterlife by ensuring that the restored name Bodhisattva remains findable and citable.

## A ‌Meditation

To contemplate Bodhisattva is to hold the idea of enlightenment Being, Compassion in the mind and to ask what of it endures. The name means "'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood ‌for the sake of all beings" — and a name that carries its meaning so openly invites meditation rather than mere recollection. The tradition remembers the name as enlightenment Being, Compassion · ‌'Awakening-being' — one who vows Buddhahood for the sake of all beings.

Sit with the restored form — Bodhisattva — and the diacritics themselves become the practice: each mark is a small ​act of attention, a refusal to let the plain ASCII form *boddhisattva* stand in for the whole. What the tradition preserved in this name, the restoration asks the reader to preserve in ‌turn.

## The Unicode Restoration

Bodhisattva aSCII-equivalent form. The ASCII fallback *boddhisattva* still resolves everywhere, but it is the restored form that carries the name's full information. Across the 12 characters of the ​name, the restoration adjusts 8: 8 further adjustments (h, i, s, a, t, v, a, a). That is the whole thesis of this temple: the marks are the message.

## Why This Restoration ​Matters

Restoring **Bodhisattva** is part of a larger effort to make the web multilingual by default. The PuniCodex project does not ask users to learn a new alphabet; it asks the infrastructure ‌to respect the alphabets that already exist. Every section of this post — the script, the sound, the myths, the evidence — converges on the same point: the marks in Bodhisattva are ​information, and information deserves an address of its own. A single Unicode domain is a small proof, but it is a proof that scales: every name restored makes the next one easier, ‌and every visit to the temple is a vote for the restored form.

## A Closer Look at the Marks

A restored name is a small map. In **Bodhisattva**, the journey ‌from the ASCII fallback *boddhisattva* to the Unicode form can be read letter by letter, and each letter tells a story. Of the 12 characters, 4 remain unchanged; they anchor the name ​to its modern shape. The remaining adjustments recover marks the source tradition used to distinguish this name from every other word built from the same letters.

The **b** stays as it is ​— Same, capitalized.

The **o** stays as it is — Same.

The **d** stays as it is — Same.

The **d** becomes **h** — Special character.

The **h** becomes **i** — Special ​character.

The **i** becomes **s** — Special character.

The **s** becomes **a** — Special character.

The **a** becomes **t** — Special character.

The **t** stays as it is — Same.

The **t** ​becomes **v** — Special character.

The **v** becomes **a** — Special character.

The **a** becomes **a** — Dropped.

Together these changes are not decoration. They are the minimum set of marks needed ‌to keep the name legible in its own tradition. Remove them and you still have a string of letters; you no longer have the name as it was written.
